assumptions.condition: For every \(j\), the conditional law of \(Y\) given \((J=j,X=x)\) has density \(f_j(\cdot\mid x)\) with respect to \(\nu\) on \(\mathcal Y\).
\(f_j(y\mid x)>0\) for every \(j\), for \(\nu\)-almost every \(y\in\mathcal Y\), and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\).

novel.justification: This proposal-specific envelope is plausible after restricting birth weight to a prespecified clinically meaningful compact range and excluding arbitrarily concentrated within-bin latent-class laws; smooth location-scale families with scales bounded away from zero and small common-support perturbations satisfy it.

assumptions.condition: \(Y\), \(A\), and \(Z\) are mutually conditionally independent given \((J,X)\).

novel.justification: This proposal-specific quantitative separation strengthens the qualitative nonsingularity used by Bian, Zhou, and Cui. In a six-bin maternal-smoking design it is plausible when the validation confusion matrix for questionnaire responses has six distinguishable columns, so no two true intensity bins induce nearly identical self-report distributions; the smallest singular value is directly diagnosable in the fitted measurement design.

This proposal-specific quantitative separation strengthens qualitative proxy nonsingularity. It is plausible when the six cotinine categories are cut at assay-calibrated thresholds whose class-conditional response profiles remain distinct across the six latent smoking intensities; a paired validation sample can screen the minimum singular value before analysis.

This proposal-specific margin requires the six latent exposure levels to induce quantitatively distinct birth-weight feature profiles, beyond qualitative factor rank. Clinically prespecified birth-weight intervals or low-order spline features can satisfy it when increasing smoking intensity shifts more than a single common mean and the six feature vectors are not nearly collinear.

This proposal-specific uniform margin strengthens the strict modal alignment used by Bian, Zhou, and Cui. For six maternal-smoking bins it is plausible when respondents are more likely to report their own intensity bin than any particular alternative by a stable amount after covariate adjustment; repeated questionnaire or validation data can estimate the modal gaps.

assumptions.condition: The smallest eigenvalue of \(R(Y,X)^{\mathsf T}D(Y,X)R(Y,X)\) is at least \(\varepsilon\) almost surely.

novel.justification: This proposal-specific margin requires the six posterior class profiles across the \(36\) self-report--cotinine cells to retain independent weighted variation at each birth-weight and covariate stratum. It is plausible when the two instruments make complementary errors and the augmented study deliberately populates every paired category through assay calibration and oversampling of discordant reports; the recovered \(R^{\mathsf T}DR\) eigenvalues provide a design diagnostic.

This proposal-specific regular-stratum condition excludes covariate strata at which residualized questionnaire or cotinine score directions appear or disappear exactly. In the six-bin augmented study it is plausible under a fixed measurement protocol and common category support, with sufficiently populated \(36\)-cell tables so the same estimable linear combinations of the \(72\) raw measurement directions persist across covariates.

assumptions.condition: Every nonzero eigenvalue of \(G(X)\) is at least \(\varepsilon\) almost surely.

novel.justification: This proposal-specific gap prevents the stable residualized measurement directions from becoming nearly collinear. In the six-bin maternal-smoking design it is plausible when self-report and cotinine retain complementary conditional variation after posterior outcome adjustment and the study enriches sparse discordant cells; the nonzero eigenvalues of the recovered conditional Gram matrix are estimable design-strength diagnostics.

definitions.name: Regular hidden ordered-treatment model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}=\{P:\ P\text{ obeys the listed member properties for fixed }K\}\)

definitions.name: Positive three-class continuous witness
definitions.construction: \(P^{\star}\) is induced by \(X\equiv0\), \(K=L=3\), \(\mathcal Y=[0,3]\), \(\pi=(0.3,0.4,0.3)^{\mathsf T}\), \(M_A=0.7I_3+0.1\mathbf 1_3\mathbf 1_3^{\mathsf T}\), \(M_Z=0.4I_3+0.2\mathbf 1_3\mathbf 1_3^{\mathsf T}\), and \(f_j(y)=\sum_{b=0}^{2}H_{bj}\mathbf 1\{b\leq y<b+1\}\), where \(H=\begin{pmatrix}0.7&0.2&0.1\\0.2&0.6&0.2\\0.1&0.2&0.7\end{pmatrix}\), \(\nu\) is Lebesgue measure, \(h_0(y)=(\mathbf 1\{0\leq y<1\},\mathbf 1\{1\leq y<2\},\mathbf 1\{2\leq y\leq3\})^{\mathsf T}\), \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}\perp J\) with marginal density \(f_j\) for \(Y(j)\), \(Y=Y(J)\), and \(A\), \(Z\), and \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}\) are mutually conditionally independent given \(J\)

definitions.name: Latent additive score image
definitions.construction: \(\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}^{\,L^{2}(P)}\), where \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is the observed conditional-expectation image of centered factor scores

definitions.name: Pointwise-cell and conditional-Gram projector
definitions.construction: Set \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w)\), \(D=\operatorname{diag}(Bw)\), and \(R=D^{-1}BW\). Define the first elimination by \(N=N_B=I_{K^{2}}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}=I_{K^{2}}-R(R^{\mathsf T}DR)^{+}R^{\mathsf T}D\), residualize the \(2K^{2}\) measurement vectors as \(h=N_Bc\), set \(G(X)=E_P(hh^{\mathsf T}\mid X)\) and \(b_{f_0}(X)=E_P\{h(N_Bf_0)\mid X\}\), and define \(Qf_0=N_Bf_0-h^{\mathsf T}G(X)^{+}b_{f_0}(X)\)

definitions.name: Exact symbolic \(K=3\) projector audit
definitions.construction: In \(\mathfrak A_3\), use \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,w_2,w_3)\) with positive nonconstant weights, \(D=\operatorname{diag}(Bw)\), \(R=D^{-1}BW\), and \(N_B=I_9-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\); verify the six matrix identities in Lemma 3A by exact symbolic multiplication and range--kernel algebra.

definitions.name: Adjacent-intensity efficiency-gain diagnostic
definitions.construction: For each \(c_j\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{adj}}\), form the recovered cell vector \(v_j\), apply the measurement-form projector \(N_B=I_{K^{2}}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\), augment \(G(X)\) to \(G_j^{\mathrm{aug}}(X)=\begin{pmatrix}G(X)&b_{v_j}(X)\\b_{v_j}(X)^{\mathsf T}&E_P\{[N_Bv_j](O)^2\mid X\}\end{pmatrix}\), and take its Schur residual \(\Lambda_j(X)=E_P\{[N_Bv_j](O)^2\mid X\}-b_{v_j}(X)^{\mathsf T}G(X)^{+}b_{v_j}(X)\)

definitions.name: Coherent cross-fitted nuisance system
definitions.construction: For each training fold, fit one label-aligned product factorization represented by \(\widehat\eta\); set \(\widehat W=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat w)\), \(\widehat B=\widehat M_A\odot\widehat M_Z\), \(\widehat d=\widehat B\widehat w\), \(\widehat D=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat d)\), \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\), \(\widehat N=I_{K^{2}}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B(\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B)^{+}\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\), \(\widehat h=\widehat N\widehat c\), and derive \(\widehat G\), \(\widehat b_{(\cdot)}\), \(\widehat b_U\), and \(\widehat Q\) from those same objects before held-out evaluation

definitions.name: Constant-\(X\) finite-feature inverse handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathfrak I_0\): when \(X\) is degenerate, differentiate the normalized three-view feature tensor and invert its separated finite Jacobian on the observed score image to recover centered scores for \(\pi\), \(M_A\), \(M_Z\), and \(\Gamma_Y\)

definitions.name: Differential factor-lifting handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathfrak I\): start from \(\mathfrak I_0\), select a measurable conditional-\(X\) finite-factor inverse with a uniform operator bound, subtract the recovered finite factor scores, and invert the remaining mixture equation for each support-preserving outcome-density score in conditional \(L^{2}\)

definitions.name: H\"older coherent-fit subclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})=\{P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}:P\text{ obeys the compact-domain and H\"older-factor member properties for }d_X,\beta,B_{\mathrm H}\}\)

definitions.name: Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen finite-partition variance sequence
definitions.construction: In the binary restriction, partition \((-L,L]\) into \(\mathcal I^{\ell}\), form \(\mathcal P_1^{\ell}=\{h\in\mathcal Q^{\ell}:E_P(h\mid J^{\mathrm{bin}},X)=0\}\), use the Supplement S8.2 conditional-probability basis \((p_1^{\ell},\ldots,p_{\ell-2}^{\ell})\), set \(V^{\ell}=(B_0p_1^{\ell},B_1p_1^{\ell},\ldots,B_0p_{\ell-2}^{\ell},B_1p_{\ell-2}^{\ell})^{\mathsf T}\), and project by \(Q_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}}f=E_P(fV^{\ell,\mathsf T})\{E_P(V^{\ell}V^{\ell,\mathsf T})\}^{-1}V^{\ell}\)

definitions.name: Coherent nuisance-rate handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathfrak F\): on \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})\), fit a single tensor-product B-spline product likelihood for \((\pi,M_A,M_Z,f)\) with \(s_n\asymp n^{(d_X+1)/(2\beta+d_X+1)}\), choose from the \(K!\) common permutations the maximizer of the empirical training-sample minimum diagonal-minus-largest-off-diagonal self-report probability, and derive \(w,W,B,d,D,R,N,h,G,b_{(\cdot)},b_U\) by the corrected plug-in Bayes and \(D\)-orthogonal projection identities

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the normalized conditional three-view tensor identifies \((\pi,M_A,M_Z,f)\) up to a common permutation, the modal margin selects the unique ordered labeling, and \(\psi_j=E_P\{m_j(X)\}=E\{Y(j)\}\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).
statements.justification: This isolates point identification from the later efficiency claim and fixes the causal meaning of each recovered class.
statements.gap: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes identify factors up to labels, while Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen give the binary hidden-treatment version; the conditional measurable \(K\)-class formulation must be verified on the stated quantitative stratum.
statements.consumer: It makes the six maternal-smoking exposure levels interpretable as ordered intervention states rather than anonymous mixture classes.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), \(\phi_j=U_j-\psi_j\) is an observed-data influence function for \(\psi_j\); it is the static, zero-discount specialization of the categorical product-bridge construction in Appendix A.8 of Bian, Zhou, and Cui.
statements.justification: The finite projection needs a valid starting gradient whose relationship to published categorical bridges is exact.
statements.gap: Bian, Zhou, and Cui provide validity but not canonicality for the present static continuous-outcome target.
statements.consumer: It lets analysts retain the multiply robust bridge architecture while replacing its avoidable variance by the canonical correction.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\) under which \(X\) is degenerate, the derivative of the normalized \(K\times K\times K\) three-view feature-tensor map has a right inverse on its observed finite-feature score image whose operator norm is bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\); applying \(\mathfrak I_0\) recovers centered scores for \(\pi\), \(M_A\), \(M_Z\), and \(\Gamma_Y\) under the modal labeling.
statements.justification: This finite-dimensional derivative inversion is the mandatory first gate before any measurable conditional-\(X\) or full-density lifting claim.
statements.gap: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes prove level uniqueness of discrete factors, while Hu and Schennach prove full-law recovery through operators; neither result states this quantitative right inverse for the finite normalized tensor derivative.
statements.consumer: It provides the constant-covariate kill test and the local inverse needed to begin the full tangent-completeness proof.

statements.statement: Starting from the constant-\(X\) finite-feature inverse \(\mathfrak I_0\), can the handle \(\mathfrak I\) be completed into a conditional-\(X\), measurable, uniformly bounded right inverse from every observed DQM score in \(\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\) to centered latent additive factor scores, including support-preserving recovery of the full class-density score?
statements.justification: This is the non-formal consequence of tensor identification on which the claimed canonicality genuinely rests.
statements.gap: Hu and Schennach identify a continuous latent full law under operator conditions, and Deaner transports that recovery to triple-proxy causal functionals; these level-identification results do not differentiate the factorization or furnish a conditional-\(X\), measurable, uniformly bounded right inverse for every observed DQM score. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes establish discrete factor uniqueness, while Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen project oracle scores in the binary model.
statements.consumer: A positive answer certifies that no unmodeled observed tangent direction invalidates the efficiency bound; a negative answer kills the canonical-gradient spine.

statements.statement: At every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the full observed-data tangent space satisfies \(\mathcal T=\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}^{\,L^{2}(P)}\), and therefore \(\mathcal T^{\perp}=\{k\in L^{2}_{0}(P):E(k\mid Y,J,X)=E(k\mid A,J,X)=E(k\mid Z,J,X)=0\}\).
statements.justification: Equality with the full observed DQM closure, not merely a convenient submodel score span, is the key efficiency theorem.
statements.gap: Continuous full-law recovery in Hu and Schennach and its triple-proxy causal use in Deaner are identification statements, not a measurable uniformly bounded inverse of the derivative of the factor map. The binary tangent calculation in Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen also does not establish that multilevel DQM lifting on the stated regular stratum.
statements.consumer: It turns the candidate variance calculation into the information bound for every regular estimator of the smoking-level contrasts.

statements.statement: Under common support, latent positivity, and observed-cell positivity, \(W\) and \(D\) are invertible; the surrogate and proxy rank conditions imply that \(B\) has full column rank. Bayes' rule gives \(R=D^{-1}BW\), \(R^{\mathsf T}D=WB^{\mathsf T}\), and \(R^{\mathsf T}DR=WB^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}BW\). Hence \(N_B=I_{K^{2}}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}=I_{K^{2}}-R(R^{\mathsf T}DR)^{+}R^{\mathsf T}D\), without any additional restriction on \(w\), and \(N_B^2=N_B\), \(N_B^{\mathsf T}D=DN_B\), \(B^{\mathsf T}N_B=0\), \(\operatorname{range}(N_B)=\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\), and \(\ker(N_B)=\operatorname{range}(D^{-1}B)=\operatorname{range}(R)\). In the exact symbolic configuration \(\mathfrak A_3\) with \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,w_2,w_3)\) and positive nonconstant \(w_j\), all six identities hold by matrix multiplication for every full-column-rank \(B\) with \(Bw>0\).
statements.justification: This algebra fixes the first outcome-score elimination and independently stress-tests it under nonuniform posterior weights.
statements.gap: The posterior-coordinate formula is valid only after the Bayes reparameterization; the required target is \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\), not the distinct cell-weighted null space \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T}D)\).
statements.consumer: It supplies an exact symbolic unit test for every implementation of the nine-cell \(K=3\) operator.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the outcome-score restrictions \(E_P(k\mid Y,J=j,X)=0\) are equivalent, cellwise, to \(B^{\mathsf T}k=0\). The operator \(N=N_B=I_{K^{2}}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\) is their pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector, \(b_{f_0}(X)\in\operatorname{range}\{G(X)\}\), and \(Qf_0=N_Bf_0-h^{\mathsf T}G(X)^{+}b_{f_0}(X)\) is the \(L^{2}(P)\)-orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal T^{\perp}\) for every \(f_0\in L^{2}(P)\).
statements.justification: The theorem eliminates the infinite continuous-outcome nuisance pointwise and leaves only one finite conditional Gram solve.
statements.gap: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen use an equal-width outcome partition and nuisance-dependent conditional-probability functions for the binary continuous-outcome projection; no located source gives this exact multilevel \(K^{2}\)-cell plus \(2K^{2}\)-Gram representation.
statements.consumer: It makes exact efficiency computation feasible without selecting an outcome sieve in the continuous birth-weight application.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(K\geq3\), the vector \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi-Q\phi\), with the first elimination \(N_B=I_{K^{2}}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\), is the unique canonical gradient for \(\psi\) in \(\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), and \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\) is the semiparametric efficiency bound. The operator uses fixed \(K^{2}\)-cell algebra and one Gram solve of dimension at most \(2K^{2}\), with no outcome-partition resolution or outcome-basis approximation index.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: an exact continuous-outcome efficiency bound with fixed finite linear algebra.
statements.gap: The closest result defines the binary continuous canonical gradient abstractly and approximates its projection; the exact multilevel projector and tangent-completeness proof are absent.
statements.consumer: It supplies the variance-minimizing regular score for all prespecified smoking-intensity contrasts.

statements.statement: In the binary restriction \(J^{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}\), let \(\mathcal I^{\ell}\), \(\mathcal Q^{\ell}\), \(\mathcal P_1^{\ell}\), the nuisance-dependent conditional-probability functions \(p_1^{\ell},\ldots,p_{\ell-2}^{\ell}\), and \(V^{\ell}=(B_0p_1^{\ell},B_1p_1^{\ell},\ldots,B_0p_{\ell-2}^{\ell},B_1p_{\ell-2}^{\ell})^{\mathsf T}\) be exactly the outcome-partition construction of Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen Supplement S8.2. With \(Q\) built from the corrected \(D\)-orthogonal first elimination \(N_B\), every well-defined \(\operatorname{span}(V^{\ell})\) is contained in \(\operatorname{range}(Q)\), and \(V_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}=E_P[\{(Q-Q_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}\{(Q-Q_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}^{\mathsf T}]\succeq0\). The gap is strict in a contrast direction \(c\) exactly when \(c^{\mathsf T}(Q-Q_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\neq0\). Along a nested equal-width refinement subsequence, the Supplement S8.2 density of \(\mathcal P_1^{\ell}\) in the binary conditional-null space implies \(Q_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\phi\to Q\phi\) in \(L^{2}(P)\) and \(V_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\to V_{\mathrm{eff}}\). This comparison is a binary restriction only; the exact fixed-cell theorem is asserted for \(K\geq3\).
statements.justification: The theorem compares the exact projection only with the comparator's actual partition-dependent, nuisance-dependent construction and separates that binary audit from the \(K\geq3\) contribution.
statements.gap: Supplement S8.2 proves density of its equal-width partition spaces and proposes the finite-\(\ell\) projection, but it does not reduce the multilevel continuous projection to fixed \(K^{2}\)-cell and \(2K^{2}\)-Gram algebra.
statements.consumer: It lets a binary-analysis user quantify the residual variance of the published discretization while preventing that binary approximation from being misrepresented as an arbitrary fixed-basis module.

statements.statement: For every adjacent maternal-smoking intensity contrast \(c_j=e_{j+1}-e_j\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{adj}}\), compute \(N_Bv_j\) with \(N_B=I_{K^{2}}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\). The recovered augmented conditional Gram matrix \(G_j^{\mathrm{aug}}(X)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}\{G_j^{\mathrm{aug}}(X)\}\leq\operatorname{rank}\{G(X)\}+1\), and the observable condition \(P_X[\operatorname{rank}\{G_j^{\mathrm{aug}}(X)\}=\operatorname{rank}\{G(X)\}+1]>0\), equivalently \(P_X\{\Lambda_j(X)>0\}>0\), certifies \(c_j^{\mathsf T}Q\phi\neq0\) and strict variance reduction for that dose step. As a supporting consequence, \(c_j^{\mathsf T}(V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}})c_j=E_P\{(c_j^{\mathsf T}Q\phi)^2\}=E_P\{\Lambda_j(X)\}>0\); more generally, \(c^{\mathsf T}(V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}})c=E_P\{(c^{\mathsf T}Q\phi)^2\}\) for every \(c\in\mathbb R^K\).
statements.justification: The conditional residual-energy diagnostic can be estimated from recovered cells and the same Gram solve, so strict gain for each adjacent exposure step is empirically certifiable rather than assumed.
statements.gap: Categorical product-bridge validity and the abstract projection formula do not provide an observable criterion for deciding which scientifically prespecified adjacent smoking-intensity contrasts receive a nonzero correction.
statements.consumer: It lets the maternal-smoking analyst report, for every neighboring pair of exposure bins, whether canonicalization yields a genuine efficiency gain.

statements.statement: On the fixed-rank spectral-gap stratum, form \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\) and \(\widehat N=I_{K^{2}}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B(\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B)^{+}\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\) from the same fitted factorization. Then \(\|\widehat N-N_B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_D+r_B)\), \(r_R+r_N+r_h+r_G+r_b=O_P(R_{\Sigma})\), and the estimated correction is linearly stable: \(\|\widehat Q\widehat U-QU\|_{L^{2}(P)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_{\Sigma}\); the full estimated efficient score has the same \(L^{2}(P)\) bound.
statements.justification: Pseudoinverse perturbation control is needed to transport nuisance rates into score convergence without differentiating the outcome-density estimator twice.
statements.gap: The adjacent bridge papers do not analyze perturbation of this nested posterior and conditional-Gram projector.
statements.consumer: It converts rates from a coherent latent-factor fit into consistent standard errors and stable contrast scores.

statements.statement: For every coherent foldwise fit using \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\) and the corrected \(\widehat N\), \(\|E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi\|\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n\), where \(\Delta_n=r_m(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z)+r_Ar_Z+(r_A+r_Z)R_{\Sigma}\); in particular, perturbing only \(M_A\) or only \(f\) has zero first-order mean bias.
statements.justification: The cancellation shows that the finite efficiency correction preserves orthogonality when all fitted objects arise from one product law.
statements.gap: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen establish mixed bias for their binary score, while the new projected \(K\)-class correction introduces posterior and Gram errors not covered by that expansion.
statements.consumer: It permits flexible learning of exposure misclassification and birth-weight regressions under explicit product-rate conditions.

statements.statement: Let every training-fold operator use \(\widehat N=I_{K^{2}}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B(\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B)^{+}\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\). If each fold satisfies \(R_{\Sigma}=o_P(1)\) and \(\Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\), then \(\sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_P(1)\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)\rightsquigarrow N(0,V_{\mathrm{eff}})\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{eff}}\).
statements.justification: The result pairs the efficiency bound with an attaining estimator and exposes every required nuisance product.
statements.gap: Bian, Zhou, and Cui prove asymptotic normality for their hidden-action estimator, and Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen treat binary hidden treatment; neither theorem covers the exact projected multilevel score and its coherent-fit remainder.
statements.consumer: It yields efficient standard errors for each latent maternal-smoking exposure mean.

statements.statement: For fixed \(q\), when \(\widehat\psi\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_C\) use the corrected coherent projector in Theorem 8, \(\sqrt n(C\widehat\psi-C\psi)\rightsquigarrow N(0,\Sigma_C)\), \(\widehat\Sigma_C\to_P\Sigma_C\), and the Gaussian maximum-\(t\) critical value computed from the correlation matrix of \(\widehat\Sigma_C\) gives simultaneous coverage converging to \(1-\alpha\) for all \(q\) coordinates of \(\theta=C\psi\).
statements.justification: The application compares several adjacent smoking levels, so scalar pointwise intervals do not answer the scientific question.
statements.gap: The closest hidden-treatment theory is centered on a binary contrast and does not provide fixed-dimensional joint maximum-\(t\) inference for ordered multilevel effects.
statements.consumer: It supports one familywise-valid assessment of all declared six-bin maternal-smoking contrasts.

statements.statement: In the binary restriction obtained by replacing \(K\geq3\) with \(J^{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}\), use \(R=D^{-1}BW\) and \(N_B=I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\). The resulting cell-and-Gram operator \(Q\) reduces to the Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen continuous-outcome orthocomplement generated by \(B_0h_1(Y,X)+B_1h_2(Y,X)\) with \(E_P(h_r\mid J^{\mathrm{bin}},X)=0\). When \(Y\) is also binary, \(Q\phi=0\) and the raw product-bridge influence function is canonical. This restriction is a comparator sanity check and is not part of the proposal's \(K\geq3\) theorem scope.
statements.justification: The reduction is a mandatory sanity check against the known binary locally nonparametric special case.
statements.gap: This is not a novelty claim; it verifies that the multilevel operator nests the published binary theory exactly.
statements.consumer: It permits direct validation of software and algebra against the published binary model before analyzing six exposure levels.

statements.statement: The explicit non-binary law \(P^{\star}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{3,0.003}\). At each outcome bin its posterior weights are positive and nonconstant, \(R=D^{-1}BW\), and the exact first elimination is \(N_B=I_9-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\). The resulting operator is evaluable from nine \((A,Z)\) cells and one conditional Gram matrix of dimension at most eighteen; \(\operatorname{rank}(G)=12\), \(Q\phi\neq0\), \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\in\mathcal T\), and \(V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}\succ0\).
statements.justification: An exact continuous witness shows that strict gain is not a hand-tuned finite-table artifact and persists on a regular neighborhood.
statements.gap: The presolve calculation is numerical and quadrature-based; the proposition requires an analytic continuous score-membership and covariance calculation.
statements.consumer: It provides a reproducible unit test and a concrete design point for calibrating a multilevel hidden-exposure study.

statements.statement: On \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})\) with \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\), can the handle \(\mathfrak F\) produce a label-stable coherent estimator using tensor-product B-splines of total dimension \(s_n\asymp n^{(d_X+1)/(2\beta+d_X+1)}\), with the common permutation chosen from the \(K!\) possibilities to maximize the empirical training-sample minimum diagonal-minus-largest-off-diagonal self-report probability, such that every coordinate \(r_m,r_\pi,r_A,r_Z,r_f,r_w,r_W,r_B,r_d,r_D,r_R,r_N,r_h,r_G,r_b\) is \(O_P(\rho_n)\) for \(\rho_n=n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d_X+1)}\)? These coordinatewise rates imply \(R_{\Sigma}=O_P(\rho_n)=o_P(1)\) and \(\Delta_n=O_P(\rho_n^2)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\), while \(w\), \(W\), \(B\), \(d\), \(D\), \(R\), \(N\), \(h\), \(G\), \(b_{(\cdot)}\), and \(b_U\) remain plug-in implications rather than separately fitted nuisances.
statements.justification: The named H\"older class, spline schedule, modal-gap label rule, and coordinatewise target rates make the implementation question falsifiable while leaving efficient inference conditional on their attainment.
statements.gap: Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin estimate repeated-measurement mixtures, while Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen use an iterative sieve method; neither analyzes the new projected score with all derived nuisances constrained to one fitted law.
statements.consumer: A construction would provide the implementable first stage for the augmented maternal-smoking analysis and prevent first-order bias from incoherent nuisance fits.

sampling_model.design: \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,Z_i,X_i)\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), with fixed \(K\) and a fixed number of cross-fitting folds.
sampling_model.units: Independent study participants with bounded continuous outcomes and pretreatment covariates.
sampling_model.treatment: \(J_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\) is latent and ordered; \(A_i\) and \(Z_i\) are paired categorical measurements.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Training-fold estimation uses one coherent label-aligned product factorization; all posterior, projector, and Gram quantities are plug-in implications of that fitted law.

tldr: For every fixed \(K\geq3\), a hidden ordered treatment is recovered from a categorical surrogate, a categorical proxy, and a bounded continuous outcome. The product-bridge influence function is converted into the exact canonical gradient by the pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(N_B=I_{K^{2}}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\) over \(K^{2}\) measurement cells and one conditional Gram solve of dimension at most \(2K^{2}\). Bayes' identity \(R=D^{-1}BW\) gives the equivalent posterior formula without restricting the positive posterior weights. In the separate binary restriction, the exact variance is weakly below the Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen Supplement S8.2 finite-partition variance, and the published refinement sequence converges to the exact bound. An exact symbolic nonconstant-weight \(K=3\) audit and the explicit continuous witness make the finite operator falsifiable and nonzero. The central gate remains the measurable uniformly bounded conditional-\(X\) extension of the constant-\(X\) finite-feature derivative inverse. Efficient cross-fitted inference remains conditional on explicit product rates.

project_justification.gap: The binary hidden-treatment literature characterizes efficiency but computes the continuous-outcome correction through the specific partition-dependent sequence in Supplement S8.2, while the categorical product-bridge literature establishes validity without observed-data canonicality. Existing continuous three-proxy full-law identification does not supply the uniformly bounded derivative inverse needed for tangent completeness.
project_justification.niche: Fixed latent cardinality, quantitative three-view separation, and paired categorical measurements make it possible to eliminate the infinite outcome nuisance pointwise and expose a finite conditional information operator.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the missing DQM tangent-completeness theorem through a constant-\(X\) finite-feature inverse followed by a measurable conditional extension, derives the exact \(D\)-orthogonal finite projector onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\) for fixed \(K\geq3\), proves its Bayes-equivalent posterior representation, relates its binary restriction to the published Supplement S8.2 outcome-partition sequence, supplies an observable strict-gain criterion for adjacent exposure contrasts and an explicit non-binary witness, and attaches coherent cross-fitted inference under explicit nuisance products.

related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) are the closest theorem-level comparator. Their Theorems 2--4 give the binary observed tangent space and influence functions. Their Supplement S8.2 continuous-\(Y\) construction partitions \((-L,L]\) into equal-width cells \(I_t^{\ell}\), defines \(p_a^{\ell}(t,X)=P(Y\in I_t^{\ell}\mid J^{\mathrm{bin}}=a,X)\), constructs the conditional-null space \(\mathcal P_1^{\ell}\) and its nuisance-dependent functions \(p_1^{\ell},\ldots,p_{\ell-2}^{\ell}\), and projects on \(V^{\ell}=(B_0p_1^{\ell},B_1p_1^{\ell},\ldots,B_0p_{\ell-2}^{\ell},B_1p_{\ell-2}^{\ell})^{\mathsf T}\). Theorem 4B compares the exact operator only to that verified binary sequence. The multilevel contribution uses the \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\) onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\), which equals the posterior representation after substituting \(R=D^{-1}BW\), followed by one \(2K^{2}\)-dimensional conditional Gram solve. Bian, Zhou, and Cui (2026) inform the raw score through their categorical inverse-feature product bridge and their qualitative nonsingularity and strict modal alignment conditions; none of their assumptions is cited for the proposal-specific uniform \(\varepsilon\) margins. Their Appendix A.8 is not claimed to be improved as a hidden-action policy-value theorem. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009) inform discrete factor identification through Kruskal uniqueness and nonparametric binning. Hu and Schennach (2008) identify a continuous latent full law under three-measurement operator conditions, and Deaner (2023) adapts that level-identification route to triple-proxy causal functionals. Neither continuous full-law recovery result establishes the object required here: first a quantitative right inverse of the constant-\(X\) finite tensor derivative, and then a conditional-\(X\), measurable, uniformly bounded extension that lifts every observed DQM score while preserving support and centering. Tsiatis and Ma (2004) inform the nuisance-score projection strategy in a different functional measurement-error model. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2016) inform coherent repeated-measurement mixture estimation. Tsybakov (2009) supplies the standard H\"older and sieve-rate framework used only to formulate the coherent-fit open question. Guo, Ogburn, and Shpitser (2026) motivate the array-decomposition efficiency gap. Bennett et al. (2023), Ghassami et al. (2026), and Cobzaru et al. (2024) delimit weak-identification, partial-identification, and sensitivity extensions rather than theorem-level targets of this core.
technical_internal_limitation: For positive nonconstant \(w\) and full-column-rank \(B\), exact algebra gives \(R=D^{-1}BW\), \(R^{\mathsf T}D=WB^{\mathsf T}\), and equality of the measurement-form and posterior-form projectors. The continuous presolve witness was reproduced with twenty-four quadrature nodes per outcome bin. It has Gram rank twelve, raw-minus-projected covariance eigenvalues approximately \((0.622,1.214,1.589)\), coherent joint perturbation bias of order \(t^{2}\), and vanishing first-order bias under surrogate-only and outcome-only perturbations. The independently differentiated finite quadrature Fisher solve differs from the projector by about \(2.1\times10^{-12}\). These checks are evidence, not a proof that the candidate lies in the full continuous tangent space.
honest_scope: The proposal's exact finite projection and canonical-gradient claims are for fixed \(K\geq3\). Proposition 10 and Theorem 4B concern only the separate binary restriction used to reproduce and compare with Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen Supplement S8.2; no arbitrary fixed-basis embedding is asserted. The first cell elimination is fixed as the \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(N_B=I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\) onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\); its posterior expression is used only through the proved identity \(R=D^{-1}BW\). The exact projection, symbolic nonconstant-weight \(K=3\) audit, constant-\(X\) finite-feature derivative inverse, conditional-\(X\) tangent-space equality, partition-sequence variance comparison, pseudoinverse stability, coherent quadratic remainder, empirical-process expansion, and continuous witness membership are all to be proved. The first kill test proves the finite derivative inverse at constant \(X\), then attempts support-preserving recovery for arbitrary bounded common-support class densities; failure of either stage invalidates canonicality. The explicit \(K=3\) law is the non-binary test at which the nine-cell operator is evaluable, has Gram rank twelve, and has nonzero projected correction. The inference theorem is conditional on explicit product rates. Open-ended Question 2 asks whether a tensor-product B-spline product likelihood on \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})\), with \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\), the displayed dimension schedule, and modal-gap label selection, attains the displayed coordinatewise rates for every primitive and derived operator component; those rates are not assumed in the model class or claimed as settled. Modal ties, changing supports, vanishing singular values, and local-to-singularity confidence sets are outside this regular-stratum version. The birth-weight study is a prospective augmented design: the published six-bin application does not itself verify the availability or conditional independence of paired self-report and cotinine measurements. The literature search was bounded and cannot exclude unpublished work, so the strict comparison is confined to accessible public theorem text.

seed_details.anchor_locations: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen, Theorems 2--4 and Supplement S8.2; Bian, Zhou, and Cui, Appendix A.8.
seed_details.question: Can the available \(K\)-class product-bridge influence function be converted into the exact continuous-outcome canonical gradient by a pointwise weighted projection over \(K^{2}\) observed cells and one conditional Gram solve of dimension at most \(2K^{2}\)?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the binary equal-width outcome-partition projection and its nuisance-dependent conditional-probability functions in Supplement S8.2 of Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen by pointwise elimination of outcome-factor scores through the \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\) onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\), and then remove the remaining measurement directions by a finite conditional Gram solve.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for hidden-treatment canonical gradients, categorical continuous outcomes, three-view tangent spaces, and finite cell projections found the binary refining-partition construction but no exact \(K\)-class continuous projector.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen because their Theorem 4 already defines the continuous-outcome efficient influence function by projection.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their continuous projection is computed from equal-width outcome partitions and nuisance-dependent conditional probabilities in a binary model; the proposed theorem derives an exact partition-free projector for fixed \(K\geq3\), proves the missing factor-score lifting, and supplies a coherent-fit quadratic remainder.

seed_details.anchor_locations: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes, Theorem 1, Corollary 2, and the proof of Theorem 8; Hu and Schennach, the main continuous measurement-error identification theorem; Deaner, Sections 2--3 on triple-proxy full-law recovery; Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen, Supplement S5.
seed_details.question: Does quantitative three-view separation imply that every observed DQM score lifts measurably to additive latent factor scores through a uniformly bounded differential inverse?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the normalized Kruskal factorization rather than only recovering its factors, invert the finite Jacobian on its image, and recover the residual outcome-density score in conditional \(L^{2}\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for differential inversion of three-view latent-class maps and semiparametric tangent completeness found discrete algebraic identification, continuous full-law recovery, and model-specific latent-class efficiency theory, but no measurable conditional-\(X\), uniformly bounded score-lifting theorem for arbitrary bounded class densities.
seed_details.red_team: Continuous full-law identification in Hu and Schennach and Deaner makes the score lifting automatic after differentiation.
seed_details.rebuttal: Level identification does not by itself control the inverse derivative. The reverse tangent inclusion additionally requires conditional-\(X\) measurability, a uniform operator bound, support-preserving paths, centering, and recovery of the infinite-dimensional class-density score.
seed_details.disposition: survives as the central open proof obligation of seed 1

seed_details.anchor_locations: Bennett et al., main strong-identification theorem and penalized minimax construction; Bian, Zhou, and Cui, Theorem 4 and Assumption 5.1.
seed_details.question: What limiting experiment and uniformly valid confidence set govern \(C\psi\) when the smallest tensor-factor or projection-Gram singular value shrinks with \(n\)?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the linear conditional-moment operator in Bennett et al. by the differential of the nonlinear tensor-factor map composed with the contrast and the tangent projection.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for weak proxies with tensor decomposition found weak proxy-SVAR and linear conditional-moment theory, not local-to-singularity inference for a nonlinear three-view factorization followed by a canonical projection.
seed_details.red_team: This is ordinary weak-instrument asymptotics after reparameterizing the smallest singular value.
seed_details.rebuttal: Two distinct nonlinear singularities enter in composition, and the low-dimensional contrast can remain regular along directions for which the latent factors are not, so the linear weak-instrument experiment is not inherited mechanically.
seed_details.disposition: survives but deferred because fixed-separation canonicality must be settled first

seed_details.red_team: Once an efficient score is available, standard empirical welfare maximization gives the regret bound verbatim.
seed_details.rebuttal: The leading regret term may be standard after score construction, and no new lower frontier is yet visible; the seed is not retained without a hidden-treatment-specific complexity or weak-separation phenomenon.

literature_map.settled: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen identify binary hidden-treatment means, characterize the observed tangent space, and approximate the continuous-outcome canonical gradient in Supplement S8.2 by equal-width partitions and nuisance-dependent conditional-probability functions spanning \(\mathcal P_1^{\ell}\).
literature_map.open_boundary: Their paper does not give the exact partition-free fixed-\(K\) cell projector for \(K\geq3\), the projection identity locating their binary finite-partition variance relative to the exact binary bound, or a multilevel coherent-fit remainder.

literature_map.settled: Bian, Zhou, and Cui construct inverse-feature bridges and a valid product-bridge influence function for \(K\) hidden action classes in Appendix A.8.
literature_map.open_boundary: They do not identify that influence function as the canonical gradient in the static continuous-outcome three-view model.

literature_map.settled: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes prove discrete uniqueness up to simultaneous label permutation under Kruskal-rank inequalities. Hu and Schennach identify continuous latent full laws under three-measurement operator conditions, and Deaner applies that recovery to triple-proxy causal functionals.
literature_map.open_boundary: These are level-identification results. They do not provide a conditional-\(X\), measurable, uniformly bounded right inverse of the differentiated factor map that recovers centered, support-preserving latent scores from every observed DQM score.

literature_map.settled: Tsiatis and Ma construct locally efficient scores by projecting a parametric score away from a nonparametric latent-covariate nuisance tangent space.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their functional measurement-error model does not contain an unidentified ordered latent treatment recovered from two categorical views and a continuous outcome factor.

literature_map.settled: Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin give constructive repeated-measurement mixture recovery, two-step estimation, and asymptotic theory.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their target is the mixture law and its plug-in functionals, not the explicit causal canonical gradient or a nuisance-orthogonal cross-fitted estimator.

literature_map.settled: Guo, Ogburn, and Shpitser compare bridge and array-decomposition assumptions and describe array-decomposition semiparametric theory as nascent.
literature_map.open_boundary: No closer paper located in their cited threads derives the proposed exact continuous projector.

literature_map.settled: Bennett et al. obtain root-\(n\) inference for strongly identified linear functionals of weakly identified conditional-moment nuisances, while Ghassami et al. derive proxy bounds when completeness fails.
literature_map.open_boundary: Neither covers a nonlinear three-view factorization composed with a finite tangent projection; these threads motivate later singular-boundary work rather than subsume the regular-stratum kernel.

novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level result is Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen: it gives the binary observed tangent space and defines the continuous-outcome efficient influence function by projection. Supplement S8.2 computes its approximation from equal-width outcome partitions, the nuisance-dependent probabilities \(p_a^{\ell}(t,X)\), the conditional-null spaces \(\mathcal P_1^{\ell}\), and the vectors \(V^{\ell}\); it is not an arbitrary fixed-basis module. Theorem 4B makes only the supported binary comparison: each finite-partition variance exceeds the exact binary bound by the covariance of the omitted projected correction and the refining sequence converges. The proposal's strict delta is separate and non-binary: for every fixed \(K\geq3\), the exact partition-free first elimination is the \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(N_B=I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{+}B^{\mathsf T}\) onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\), not a projector onto \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T}D)\). Bayes' formula \(R=D^{-1}BW\), with positive invertible \(W\), proves its equivalent posterior representation without any restriction that posterior weights be constant. The remaining measurement directions require one Gram system of dimension at most \(2K^{2}\). The exact symbolic \(K=3\) audit with positive nonconstant posterior weights verifies idempotence, \(D\)-self-adjointness, the range and kernel identities, and the posterior reparameterization; the explicit \(K=3\) continuous law shows that the full operator is evaluable and nonzero. Bian, Zhou, and Cui already supply the \(K\)-class inverse-feature product bridge and qualitative nonsingularity and alignment, so neither the bridge nor the qualitative conditions are claimed as new; all uniform spectral and modal margins are proposal-specific regular-stratum assumptions. Hu and Schennach identify a continuous latent full law, and Deaner uses that recovery for triple-proxy causal functionals; neither result supplies the required constant-\(X\) quantitative inverse of the finite tensor derivative followed by a conditional-\(X\), measurable, uniformly bounded right inverse for full observed DQM scores. The remaining contributions are the observable strict-gain diagnostic for adjacent exposure contrasts and the coherent-factorization quadratic remainder.
